description: Health dashboard for containerized AAP 2.5/2.6 on RHEL. Uses Prometheus metrics from /api/controller/v2/metrics/ plus json_exporter metrics (aap_service_status / aap_redis_info) scraped from /api/gateway/v1/status/. Requires json_exporter on the Gateway VM. See json_exporter/README.md for setup. No Grafana Infinity plugin required.

panels.title: Gateway Status
panels.description: Platform Gateway health from /api/gateway/v1/status/ (services.gateway.status). Requires Grafana Infinity datasource pointed at the AAP Gateway with a Bearer token.

panels.title: Controller Status
panels.description: Automation Controller health from /api/gateway/v1/status/ (services.controller.status).

panels.title: Hub Status
panels.description: Automation Hub health from /api/gateway/v1/status/ (services.hub.status). Shows N/A if Hub is not installed.

panels.title: EDA Status
panels.description: Event-Driven Ansible health from /api/gateway/v1/status/ (services.eda.status). Shows N/A if EDA is not installed.

panels.title: Redis Status
panels.description: Centralized Redis health from /api/gateway/v1/status/ (services.redis.status). Complements the Controller-observed Redis queue panels below.

panels.title: Redis Mode
panels.description: Redis deployment mode from /api/gateway/v1/status/ (services.redis.mode): standalone or cluster.

Inferred from the Prometheus up metric for the scrape of /api/controller/v2/metrics/. In AAP 2.5/2.6 the scrape goes through the Platform Gateway, so UP means the Gateway path to the Controller metrics endpoint is succeeding. This is not a Gateway-native health metric. DOWN may mean Gateway, Controller, network, or auth failure.
panels.title: Gateway / API Reachable

panels.description: Count of control-plane nodes registered with the Controller (node_type control or hybrid) from awx_instance_info.
panels.title: Controller Nodes Online

panels.description: Count of execution nodes registered with the Controller (node_type=execution) from awx_instance_info. Reflects Controller mesh registration, not OS-level health.
panels.title: Execution Nodes Online

panels.description: Count of hop nodes registered with the Controller (node_type=hop) from awx_instance_info. Zero is normal when no hop nodes are deployed.
panels.title: Hop Nodes Online

panels.description: Number of active user sessions reported by the Controller (awx_sessions_total type=user).
panels.title: Active User Sessions

panels.description: All mesh nodes registered with the Controller: control, hybrid, execution, and hop. Data from awx_instance_info (hostname, node_type, version, enabled).
panels.title: Registered Nodes

panels.description: Percentage of capacity consumed per registered mesh node (control, hybrid, execution, hop). Green < 70%, yellow 70-90%, red >= 90%.
panels.title: Capacity by Node

panels.description: Remaining execution capacity (fork slots) available per registered mesh node. Low values indicate the node is near its execution limit.
panels.title: Remaining Capacity by Node

panels.description: Controller-observed PostgreSQL connectivity: UP when awx_database_connections_total > 0. This is NOT the Operator dashboard's independent Grafana SELECT 1 probe — it only proves the Controller currently has open DB connections via /api/controller/v2/metrics/. If the metrics scrape is down, this may show DOWN even if PostgreSQL is up.
panels.title: PostgreSQL Accessible

panels.description: Controller-observed PostgreSQL application health from connections and latency. UP when connections are active and latency is normal; DEGRADED when commit > 1s or event processing avg > 2s; DOWN when no connections are reported. Depends on the Controller metrics scrape.

targets.expr: (clamp_max(sum(awx_database_connections_total{job=~"$service",instance=~"$instance"}), 1) * (1 + clamp_max(((avg(task_manager_commit_seconds{job=~"$service",instance=~"$instance"}) > bool 1) or (avg(callback_receiver_event_processing_avg_seconds{job=~"$service",instance=~"$instance"}) > bool 2)), 1))) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: PostgreSQL Health

panels.description: Controller-observed Redis reachability for the callback-receiver event queue. UP when callback_receiver_events_queue_size_redis is present (Controller can read the Redis queue). This is NOT Redis Cluster replica/StatefulSet health (those require Kubernetes metrics). Does not detect Redis cluster_state failures where the metric still reports.
panels.title: Redis Reachable

panels.description: Depth of the callback-receiver Redis event queue. Growing values indicate events waiting to be written to PostgreSQL. Shows 0 when idle. Not a Redis cluster replica count.
panels.title: Redis Event Queue Depth

panels.description: Number of automation jobs currently executing across all controller instances.
panels.title: Running Jobs

panels.description: Jobs waiting in the queue to be picked up by a controller task worker. High pending count may indicate capacity issues.
panels.title: Pending Jobs

panels.description: Total number of jobs that ended in 'failed' or 'error' status. A rising count may indicate playbook issues or infrastructure problems.
panels.title: Failed Jobs

panels.description: Jobs blocked by dependency constraints (e.g., waiting for a parent workflow node to complete). High blocked count may indicate workflow design issues or a failed upstream job holding the pipeline.
panels.title: Blocked Tasks

panels.description: Percentage of total controller capacity (fork slots) currently consumed by running jobs. Yellow at 70%, red at 90% -- indicates the controller is running out of execution capacity.
panels.title: Consumed Capacity

panels.description: Time-series breakdown of all job statuses over time: Running, Successful, Failed, Error, Canceled, Waiting, Pending, and Blocked.
panels.title: Job Launched Statistics

panels.description: Processing time for the controller task manager. High values indicate the controller is slow to load or start tasks.
panels.title: Controller Processing Time

panels.description: Time spent on PostgreSQL-related Controller work: committing task state, loading pending/workflow tasks, and average callback event processing time. Do NOT use callback_receiver_events_insert_db_seconds (legacy 'Saving Events to DB') — that series is a cumulative total and can show multi-hour values. Use Event Processing Avg (callback_receiver_event_processing_avg_seconds) instead.
panels.title: PostgreSQL Transaction Latency

panels.description: Time spent in the task manager processing pipeline: loading, starting, and processing running and pending tasks. High values indicate job scheduling bottlenecks.
panels.title: Task Manager Execution Time

panels.description: Total active PostgreSQL connections reported by the Controller metrics endpoint. Red at 0 (no connections), yellow at 1-2 (thin pool), green at 3 or more.
panels.title: DB Connections

panels.description: Callback receiver metrics: Redis event queue depth (events waiting to be written to DB), events held in memory, and average processing time per event. A growing queue indicates the system cannot keep up with event volume. Shows 'No data' when no jobs are running and the callback receiver is idle.
panels.title: Event Processing (Callback Receiver)
